knowledge.title: {{product}} — knowledge wiki
knowledge.unresolved: This reference was not checked against the graph.
knowledge.noPage: The manifest declares no page for kind {{kind}}.
knowledge.ungroundedHint: A statement with no footnote is not shown as fact. Whoever wrote the page grounds it, or removes it.
knowledge.blockProblem: The :::{{block}} block could not be drawn
knowledge.nothingOfKind: Nothing of this kind is in the graph yet.
knowledge.fillRunningTitle: The fill is reading the code
knowledge.fillLive: Pages appear and update here as commits are read. You can open any page now.
knowledge.emptyConnected: Start the fill to read the code repositories ({{repositories}}) into this product's graph. Pages appear here as commits are read.
knowledge.emptyNoRepository: The product has no code repository yet. Connect one, then start the fill:
knowledge.incomplete: The graph holds only part of the repository's history: a fill stopped before its last commit. Pages show what was read. Continue the fill to read the rest.
knowledge.overviewFilled: No home page is written yet. The pages below come from the graph; an agent writes the product and domain pages as Markdown in the product repository.
knowledge.overviewEmpty: Nothing is known about this product yet.
knowledge.fromMarkdown: Markdown pages of the product repository
knowledge.fromGraph: Read from the code by the fill
knowledge.noManifestTitle: This product has no kinds manifest
knowledge.noManifest: The starter set could not be written into this product, so the wiki has no kinds to show. The files {{file}} and templates/ are what it reads.

writer.notInstalled: Its adapter is not installed: pressing the button below installs {{package}} {{version}} (about {{size}}) into {{folder}}.
writer.notSignedIn: {{agent}} has no sign-in here: sign in with {{agent}} itself first, or its units will fail and say so.
writer.noAgentNote: The fill reads the code only. You can choose an agent after it.
writer.bound: The agent works in units: one for the product page, then one for each domain that page names (at most {{domains}}). Each unit is bound by {{turns}} turns, {{minutes}} minutes, {{calls}} tool calls and {{attempts}} refused writes; it can read the graph and write its own page, and nothing else. Nothing runs an agent until you press the button.
writer.startWith: Start the fill and let {{agent}} write the pages
writer.offerTitle: Let an agent write the product pages
writer.offerDescription: The graph is filled from the code. An agent can now write the product page and one page per domain, each statement grounded in the graph. Choose the agent, then press the button; the pages appear as each unit writes.
writer.offerNeedsAgent: Choose Claude Code or Codex to let an agent write.
writer.waitingTitle: {{agent}} writes the pages after the fill
writer.waiting: The code fill is running. When it ends, the agent starts on the product page without another press.
writer.live: Each page appears in the wiki the moment its unit writes it. You can open any page now.
writer.doneDescription: The pages are Markdown files in the product repository, under docs/. Open the home page to read them.
writer.pendingTitle: The agent has not written this page yet; the link opens when its unit has.
writer.languageNote: The agent writes every sentence and heading in this language; keys, paths and identifiers stay as they are. Changing it writes the pages again.

knowledge.refreshNote: “Refresh” reads the code again from the new commits and checks the links of the pages. The agent then edits only the pages that need it (listed above), keeping every sentence whose grounds did not change; with a new language it translates all pages. Each unit is bound by {{turns}} turns and {{minutes}} minutes.

reset.title: Start {{product}} over?
reset.store: the product's graph store, which the next fill builds again from the code;
reset.noPages: no page: the agent has written none.
reset.keeps: It keeps every other file of the product, the code repositories under repos/ and the choice of the agent. The wiki then shows the empty page.
reset.keptPages: Pages in those places that a person wrote stay: {{list}}.

knowledge.documentsMissing: The documents could not be listed
knowledge.findingsHelp: The page reads as it is. These are places where a statement points to a document, file or function that is not in the graph or the documents right now; they are marked in the text. The agent puts them right when it updates the pages; Refresh checks the links again meanwhile.
knowledge.starterSetTitle: The starter set was written into this product
knowledge.starterSet: The product had no kinds manifest, so the wiki gave it the starter set: {{files}}. They are ordinary files of the product: edit them to change the pages.
knowledge.fillPhasePoints: Reading the code of the chosen points
knowledge.catalogueIntro: The kinds of things this product's wiki works with: what each is, how many there are, how they got here, and where to see them.
knowledge.statementOpen: Open the statement with its grounds
knowledge.statementUngroundedTitle: This sentence has no ground: nothing in the graph or the documents is cited for it. Click to see it.
knowledge.statementNoGrounds: This sentence has no ground. Nothing in the graph or the documents is cited for it, so the wiki does not show it as a fact.
knowledge.statementNoExcerpt: Nothing to show from this ground: it names an entity, not lines of text.
knowledge.statementCorrectionNote: Say what is wrong and why. The correction is saved as a file in the product repository under your git name and email, marked local, not verified. The agent takes it into account when it edits this page at the next refresh.
knowledge.cutShown: The excerpt is cut; the whole file is one click away.

refNote.groundedWith: grounded with it on the page {{page}}

knowledge.statementRelying: Other statements that rely on the same grounds
knowledge.statementCorrectionUnnamed: This sentence has no name on its page yet, so a correction cannot point at it: the agent names its statements when it writes the page again.
knowledge.statementCorrectionDone: The correction is saved in {{file}}. See it under

brokenWhy.noEntity: Nothing in the graph or among the product pages is called "{{key}}".
brokenWhy.noPath: The document link has no file name.
brokenWhy.noDocument: There is no document "{{path}}" in the product repository or the code repositories.

diagram.hint: Click a box to open its page. The plus opens a box's own neighbours. Drag to move; Ctrl and the wheel, or the buttons, to zoom.
diagram.unordered: From here the graph holds no order against the steps above.
diagram.noChain: No route or function of the graph leads here, so there is no chain to draw.
diagram.emptyChain: The chain from here reaches nothing the graph records.
diagram.noSystem: The graph holds no service yet.
diagram.noModules: The graph holds no module of this service.
diagram.noFiles: The graph holds no file with lines to draw.
diagram.areaIsLines: Area is the lines of the file.
diagram.heatIsChurn: Warmer is more often changed (up to {{max}} commits).
diagram.foldedSteps: {{count}} steps inside one lane or one file are folded.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.lead_one: {{count}} term, each with the place it is stated.
glossary.lead_other: {{count}} terms, each with the place it is stated.
glossary.empty: This product has no glossary yet. A glossary is a document whose list items start with a bold term; the manifest names it under terms.
glossary.ambiguousNoNote: The documents use this word for more than one thing.
glossary.lead_few: {{count}} terms, each with the place it is stated.
glossary.lead_many: {{count}} terms, each with the place it is stated.

roles.cardTitle: Which role do you read as?
roles.cardLead: The wiki keeps one page for everyone. Your role chooses which parts of a page are open and which groups come first; the rest stays one click away.
roles.cardNote: Kept on this machine, for every product. You can switch it at the top at any time. Skipping reads everything.
roles.menuTitle: Choose the role you read as

about.product: What the product is, for whom, and what it does.
about.analyst: Requirements, use cases, rules and how they connect.
about.architect: Services, modules, contracts and how they depend on one another.
about.developer: Code: files, functions, callers and tests.
about.operations: How it runs: configuration, images, deployment and pipelines.
about.tester: What to check: use cases, rules, tests and known failures.
about.everything: Every part of every page open, in the product's own order.

loop.questionsIntro: What the agent could not settle from the code and the documents: two sources that disagree, a word used two ways, behaviour no document describes. Answer one; the next refresh edits the pages it touches and the question shows as closed by that rewrite.
loop.noQuestions: No questions yet. The agent asks one when it finds two sources that disagree or a term that means two things.
loop.questionsMissing: The questions could not be read
loop.unreadableFiles: Question files that could not be read
loop.askedBy: Asked by the agent, {{when}}, while writing
loop.waitsForRefresh: the next refresh uses the answer
loop.answerPlaceholder: Say what is true, in your own words. The agent will state it on the pages this question touches.
loop.answerWhere: The answer is saved in {{file}} in the product repository and committed under your git name and email. It is marked local, not verified.
loop.notCommitted: The answer was saved but not committed.
loop.verifiedHint: On a local install the author is whatever git says; nothing has checked it.
loop.answerWaiting: The answer is saved. The next refresh edits the pages this question touches, using it.
loop.answerClosed: Closed {{when}}: a refresh used this answer on
loop.problemsIntro: What is wrong with the pages: statements people marked as wrong, and what the engine found itself. Each says who fixes it.
loop.noProblems: No problems. Every ground and link resolves and nobody has recorded a correction.
loop.problemsMissing: The problems could not be read

problem.correction: A person says this statement is wrong
problem.ground-removed: A statement stands on something that is gone
problem.broken-link: A link or ground names nothing
problem.unplaced: An answer or correction reaches no page

whoFixes.correction: The agent fixes it at the next refresh: it edits this page using the reason above, and the correction shows as fixed.
whoFixes.ground-removed: The agent fixes it at the next refresh: it grounds the sentence on something that still exists, or drops it.
whoFixes.broken-link: The agent fixes it at the next refresh, when it edits this page.
whoFixes.unreadable-file: A person fixes it: open the file at the line shown and correct it; the wiki reads it again at once.
whoFixes.unplaced: A person fixes it: name a page in the file's "about", or add the page.

plan.title: What the refresh will do
plan.nothing: Nothing needs the agent: no ground changed, no answer or correction is waiting, and the language is the same. The refresh reads the code again and checks the links.
plan.leaves_one: {{count}} page stays as it is and costs no agent run.
plan.leaves_few: {{count}} pages stay as they are and cost no agent run.
plan.leaves_many: {{count}} pages stay as they are and cost no agent run.
plan.leaves_other: {{count}} pages stay as they are and cost no agent run.
plan.commits_one: {{count}} commit has not been read yet. The refresh reads it first, and pages whose grounds it changes join this list.
plan.commits_few: {{count}} commits have not been read yet. The refresh reads them first, and pages whose grounds they change join this list.
plan.commits_many: {{count}} commits have not been read yet. The refresh reads them first, and pages whose grounds they change join this list.
plan.commits_other: {{count}} commits have not been read yet. The refresh reads them first, and pages whose grounds they change join this list.
plan.reading: Working out which pages the refresh touches…

journal.title: How the agent wrote this page
journal.intro: Every call the agent made while it wrote this page, and every request the core refused, as the core recorded them. The journal is kept on this machine, not in the product repository.
journal.none: No journal for this page. It was written before the core kept one, or no agent has written it on this machine.
journal.failed: The journal could not be read
journal.cut: The response was cut: {{size}} bytes in all, the first part is kept.
journal.unreadable: Lines of the journal that could not be read
journal.otherRuns: Other runs that wrote this page
journal.agentAsked_many: The agent asked {{count}} questions: they are on the Questions page.
journal.taskDocsWrong: Code is right; the document is out of date
journal.taskCodeWrong: The document is right; code needs to change
journal.basisWillChange: This ground is planned to change
